title: MTV International rebrand, 2015
lede: MTV’s international on-air identity of June 2015, which critics described as pastel, badly 3D-modelled, and borrowed from vaporwave and seapunk.
summary: Broadcast identity with pastel 3D idents, drawn from Tumblr microcultures. June 2015.

source.label: Motherboard: What the Hell Is MTV’s New Rebrand About?

creator.name: MTV International (creative lead Sean Saylor, per Motherboard)

evidence.note: Relies on Motherboard and Wikipedia. No still or video of the idents was inspected.

styles.note: The best-documented corporate adoption: Wikipedia says the rebrand was “heavily inspired by vaporwave and seapunk.” Its appearance is documented, not observed here.

context: Clinton Nguyen, Motherboard, June 25, 2015: the new look is “pastel-swatched, bad 3D modeling, and visual features drawn directly from Tumblr-born microcultures,” with the slogan changed to “I am my MTV.” Sean Saylor, MTV’s vice-president of creative and marketing, is quoted on refreshing the look constantly. [Motherboard](https://www.vice.com/en/article/53989n/what-the-hell-is-mtvs-new-rebrand-about).

Wikipedia: on the same day that MTV International introduced the rebrand, Tumblr launched Tumblr TV “with an explicitly MTV-styled visual spin.” Motherboard’s Jordan Pearson wrote that the style’s cynical impulse is “co-opted and erased.” [Wikipedia: Vaporwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaporwave).
interpretation: The point at which the style became a brand look for the kind of company it satirised. The criticism is part of the record: a corporate use of vaporwave reads as either knowing or tone-deaf.
